item.title: Yacht captain on reality show 'Below Deck' arrested in Turkey after teenager dies
item.description:
Yacht captain on reality show 'Below Deck' arrested in Turkey after teenager dies
A participant from the U.S. reality TV show “Below Deck” has been arrested in Turkey following a fight in Bodrum that left a 17-year-old deadByThe Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 7:38 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
ISTANBUL -- A participant in the U.S. reality TV show “Below Deck” has been arrested in Turkey over a fight in the resort city of Bodrum that left a 17-year-old dead, local media reported Thursday.
Joao Franco, 36, and his brother Carlos allegedly became involved in an altercation with shopkeepers in Bodrum last Saturday evening, according to the private Demiroren News Agency.
Franco, whom the agency identified as a yacht captain, appeared in the Bravo channel’s “Below Deck Down Under” and “Below Deck Mediterranean” from 2018, as well as “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City.”
“Below Deck” follows the lives of crew members aboard luxury yachts as they interact with each other and their guests.
The brothers were intoxicated and an argument broke out when they started swearing, Demiroren reported. During the subsequent fight, teenager Muhammet Koyabakan fell and hit his head on the ground. He was taken to a hospital but died on Monday.

The Franco brothers, who are Portuguese nationals, were detained and later formally arrested.
News reports did not specify the charges against them, but Demiroren said they told police they were attacked and acted in self-defense. They denied hitting Koyabakan.
Bodrum, a port city on the Aegean Sea, is a favored spot for wealthy yacht owners. Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos are among the billionaires who have visited in recent years.

item.title: London court finds 2 Iranian men guilty of spying for Tehran
item.description:
London court finds 2 Iranian men guilty of spying for Tehran
Two Iranian men have been found guilty of spying on journalists in London for TehranByThe Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 7:27 AM
LONDON -- Two Iranian men who spied on journalists working for a Persian-language broadcaster in London were found guilty Thursday of spying for Tehran.
Jurors at Woolwich Crown Court in south London found Mostafa Sepahvand, 41 and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, to be working on behalf of the Iranian state and convicted of assisting a foreign intelligence service.
A third defendant, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was acquitted of all offenses against him.
“This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime,” said Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service’s special crime and counter-terrorism division.
He said the pair were promised rewards to send intelligence back to Iran, while Sepahvand was willing to go beyond surveillance to commit serious violence against their targets.

Share
PARIS -- Paris police said Thursday that armed robbers held up a jewelry store in the French capital before fleeing on motorcycles.
No one was injured.
The robbery took place around 11:15 a.m. in the city’s central 2nd arrondissement, police said in a statement to The Associated Press.
The robbers displayed weapons but did not use them, police said.

item.title: Spain approves housing measures after huge protests. Duration may depend on election
item.description:
Spain approves housing measures after huge protests. Duration may depend on election
Spain’s interim lower house of parliament has ratified housing measures designed to limit evictions and real estate speculationByJOSEPH WILSON Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 7:05 AM
Share
BARCELONA, Spain -- Spain’s interim lower house of parliament on Thursday ratified housing measures designed to limit evictions and real estate speculation, a day after a general strike and major street protests over the country’s housing cost crunch.
The duration of the approved measures, however, will likely depend on the outcome of a national election set for later this month.
The leading opposition party, the conservative Popular Party, has said that it will repeal the housing measures of the left-wing government if it takes power, which polls indicate is a real possibility.
“Yesterday, the right to housing won on the street and in workplaces, and I hope it will win again at the ballot box,” interim Housing Minister Isabel Rodríguez told lawmakers, in reference to Wednesday’s general strike and the upcoming election on Nov. 29.
Spain’s government had tried to push through the measures in October after public anger over soaring rents erupted following the nationally-televised eviction and subsequent death of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid.
But the PP and other conservative parties aligned in parliament to reject the measures. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez responded days later by calling an early election.
The government then waited to try again to pass the measures with a smaller interim parliament, where it and aligned progressive parties had a slightly more favorable distribution of seats.
The government split the measures into two decrees, with one measure that appeared doomed from the start being separated into a second decree so as not to put the rest in danger.

item.title: Scandal-hit Jensen Huang loses his shine in his birthplace Taiwan
item.description:
Scandal-hit Jensen Huang loses his shine in his birthplace Taiwan
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's image in his birthplace, Taiwan, has been tainted after the FBI began investigating his affair with an alleged Chinese agentByTAIJING WU Associated Press and JOHNSON LAI Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 6:18 AM
Share
TAIPEI, Taiwan -- TAIPEI, Taiwan (AP) — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been widely adored like a rock star in his birthplace, Taiwan. That image is now tainted after the FBI began an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese agent.
Like the rest of the world, the island was shocked by the scandal over Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman reportedly described as a Chinese spy by U.S. officials. A video of the pair visiting a restaurant in the capital city of Taipei in 2025 went viral and was broadcast globally.
The 63-year-old poster boy for the artificial intelligence revolution was born in Taiwan and spent his early years there before he moved to the United States for his schooling. He regularly visits Taiwan for business events.
Jane Hsieh’s tofu pudding shop was one of many restaurants and stores in Taipei that proudly displayed photos of Jensen Huang visiting their premises. Hsieh, 70, was first shocked by the dramatic headlines and felt deep regret for him, saying Huang used to have a near-perfect public image.
She wondered whether people would still be as warm to him as before if he returned to Taiwan again.
“If he comes into my shop again as a customer, I’d be fine, but I think it would be awkward because he’s no longer the familiar person we used to know," she said. “I’d be polite to him, but my feelings toward him would be different.”
Resident Jeff Huang, 72, noted some customers were already suggesting the removal of Huang’s photos in shops.
“He used to be very popular, but after his personal moral scandal and allegations of corporate espionage came out, he instantly fell from grace,” he said.

item.title: Far-right UK activist pleads guilty to slashing migrant dinghy in the English Channel
item.description:
Far-right UK activist pleads guilty to slashing migrant dinghy in the English Channel
A British anti-immigration activist has pleaded guilty to slashing a migrant dinghy in the English Channel while a rescuer was aboardByThe Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 6:05 AM
Share
LONDON -- A British anti-immigration activist who has led protests against migrants crossing the English Channel pleaded guilty Thursday to slashing a dinghy while a rescuer was still aboard.
Daniel Thomas, 37, pleaded guilty in Portsmouth Crown Court to criminal damage.
Social media video of the Sept. 22 incident showed Thomas taking a knife to an inflatable boat, which had no migrants aboard but was occupied by a French rescue services member.
“This is what needs to happen to everyone in these boats," Thomas said. "This is England. Get off the boat, you have time to get off the boat. This is not France. Take them back.”
Successive U.K. governments have struggled to stop people — more than 41,000 last year — making the dangerous journey across one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes.
The issue has been depicted as a crisis by politicians including Nigel Farage of the hard-right party Reform UK, and has been used as a rallying point by anti-immigration activists. Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s center-left government says stepped-up law enforcement cooperation between the United Kingdom and France has helped reduce the number of people making the crossing so far this year by more than 40% compared to 2025.
Thomas, founder of a group called Patriot Platform, has taken a leading role in a new tactic to confront police and rescuers in an attempt to try to stop small boats from landing on English shores.
The confrontational protests have drawn large groups of masked men in black who blocked the port of Dover, southeast England, in September and days later clashed with police as they tried to stop migrants being taken ashore in Portsmouth on the country’s south coast.

item.title: 10th suspect arrested in South Africa over alleged bid to fight in Russia-Ukraine war
item.description:
10th suspect arrested in South Africa over alleged bid to fight in Russia-Ukraine war
Authorities have arrested a 10th person for violating South African mercenary laws by attempting to travel to Russia to fight in the war between Russia and UkraineByMOGOMOTSI MAGOME Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 5:07 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
JOHANNESBURG -- A 10th person has been arrested on suspicion of violating South African mercenary laws by trying to travel to Russia from South Africa to fight in the war in Ukraine, authorities said Thursday.
Nine other people were arrested this week as part of a joint investigation between Interpol and South African police into recruitment drives for the war.
Five of the suspects appeared in the Kempton Park Magistrates Court on Tuesday, and prosecutors indicated that they would oppose their bail applications.
The other four were expected in court Thursday after they were arrested at a hotel in Johannesburg while preparing to board flights to Russia, according to police spokesperson Katlego Mogale.
The first nine suspects have been identified as Zimbabwean nationals. Prosecutors said Tuesday that five of them had provided Zimbabwean addresses when they were processed. They will face charges relating to violations of South Africa’s Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which prohibits mercenary activity and regulates military assistance to parties in foreign conflicts, including recruitment and training.
Several groups of South Africans have been repatriated after saying they were duped into fighting on the front lines in Ukraine. They said they were initially promised to receive security training in Russia. Reports from other African countries said many were enticed with promises of lucrative jobs and generous benefits through false advertising on social media platforms. Authorities have arrested several people in South Africa for allegedly facilitating the recruitments.

item.title: For Ethiopian mothers sheltering in Kenya, safety brings a struggle to feed children
item.description:
For Ethiopian mothers sheltering in Kenya, safety brings a struggle to feed children
Ethiopian mothers fleeing violence into Kenya have found safety but struggle to feed their childrenByDESMOND TIRO Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 4:05 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
MOYALE, Kenya -- Ethiopian mothers who fled fighting into Kenya have found safety but are struggling to feed their children, relying on communal meals and sleeping on floors as more families cross the border seeking help.
The families are fleeing fighting between Somali and Oromo communities in southern Ethiopia. The violence stems from a longstanding territorial dispute between Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regional administrations and has driven tens of thousands of people across the border into Kenya.
“We came here on foot late in the night, running for our lives, and arrived with very little,” said Shukria Dalacha, 26, whose daughter, Sijra Bonaiyo, was five days old when they crossed the border. “We do not have the means to sustain our families.”
For Dalacha, reaching safety has meant sleeping on the floor and relying on rice and beans provided to families awaiting registration. She said she was struggling to produce enough breast milk and worried about feeding her newborn.
The border violence adds to Ethiopia’s wider instability, including renewed fighting in Tigray and an insurgency in Amhara. Seven opposition groups formed an alliance in September seeking to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.
The 2020-2022 war in northern Tigray caused about 500,000 civilian deaths from violence, famine and the collapse of health services, according to researchers at Ghent University in Belgium.
Conflict has also left communities less able to withstand drought. A September assessment by regional and federal disaster authorities and humanitarian partners estimated that 3.9 million people in Tigray would need emergency food assistance through December. item.title: Dutch coalition near collapse as 1 party is upset over tax deal with opposition
item.description:
Dutch coalition near collapse as 1 party is upset over tax deal with opposition
Prime Minister Rob Jetten's Dutch coalition appears close to collapseByMIKE CORDER Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 3:26 AM
THE HAGUE, Netherlands -- The ruling Dutch three-party minority coalition led by Prime Minister Rob Jetten appeared close to collapse Thursday, less than nine months into its four-year term, as a deal to support a tax plan for next year angered one of the coalition parties.
Jetten’s centrist D66 party and the center-right Christian Democrats reached the deal Wednesday with two center-left opposition parties to get the tax package — a crucial part of the annual government budget — through the Dutch parliament.
But fellow coalition member the right-wing People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy, or VVD, slammed it as a bad deal for the Netherlands and a breach of the coalition agreement the three parties hammered out in weeks of negotiations.
Jetten skipped a European Union leaders' summit in Ireland to attend a debate in parliament about the tax measures.
The parties that agreed the deal say it raises tax on the wealthy and cuts taxes for people with low incomes. PRO called that aspect of the deal a “millionaire's tax.”
After a meeting Wednesday night, VVD leader Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius, who is also the Dutch defense minister, said her party was ambushed “by the fact that our coalition partners struck a deal with an opposition party.”
She called it “a poor proposal. Furthermore, it runs counter to the coalition agreement.”
She said that if the other coalition partners voted for the deal after the parliamentary debate Thursday, “we will at least need a fundamental reset.”
Ruben Brekelmans, the leader of the VVD's bloc in the lower house, said that a "very fundamental discussion has to take place within the coalition regarding the way forward."

item.title: Mongolia protests Malaysia’s handling of a 20-year-old murder case
item.description:
Mongolia protests Malaysia’s handling of a 20-year-old murder case
Mongolia has lodged a diplomatic protest with Malaysia over the handling of a murder case involving a Mongolian womanByEILEEN NG Associated PressNovember 12, 2026, 3:12 AM
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia -- Mongolia has lodged a diplomatic protest with Malaysia over the handling of the murder case of a Mongolian woman, urging authorities to ensure a fair legal process and provide answers to her family 20 years after her killing.
Altantuya Shaariibuu was shot dead and blown up with military-grade plastic explosives in a jungle outside Kuala Lumpur in October 2006. Her killing touched off a scandal linked to former Prime Minister Najib Razak, who has repeatedly denied any involvement.
Two members of an elite police unit who were Najib’s bodyguards were convicted of killing Altantuya. Her lover Abdul Razak Baginda, a close aide to Najib, was tried but acquitted of abetting the crime. Who ordered the killing was never established. Altantuya was 28 and pregnant at the time of her death.
Former Mongolian Prime Minister Zandanshatar Gombojav said Thursday that Mongolia “profoundly regret the decision” in January by Malaysia’s Court of Appeal that removed the Malaysian government’s liability in a civil suit brought by Altantuya’s family and reduced the damages awarded.
Zandanshatar is Mongolia's special envoy and a member of a high-level government task force to support Altantuya's family.
He said Mongolia had sent a diplomatic protest note on Tuesday with four requests: including a fair review of the court ruling, the return of a convicted officer who escaped to Australia so he can testify in the civil suit, an examination of potentially new evidence and an official written response to Mongolia.
